{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjccM8AAAABZgnEaw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IfzhDHr3c", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3If", "number": 51, "title": "Correct V30MZ PUSH SP value sampling in both register encodings", "body": "## Problem

At baseline `9b98c69f59b736e4c31df5414844466e8ba3a099`, `crates/ws-core/src/cpu.rs:421` and `:705–707` sample SP before `push` decrements it at `:176–177`. Consequently, both `54` and `FF F4` store the incoming SP instead of the decremented value.

Static reproduction, not executed during planning: with SS=`0000`, SP=`2000`, either encoding stores `2000` at `0000:1FFE`; expected stored value is `1FFE`. A following `POP AX` exposes the incorrect value. Software using this instruction to obtain or pass a stack address receives an address displaced by two bytes. Commercial-title impact remains unmeasured.

## Expected outcome

For both encodings, decrement SP by two with 16-bit wrapping, then store that updated SP through the existing SS-based word-write path. Preserve FLAGS, other registers, instruction continuation and existing accounting. Apply the rule across emulated Mono/Color/SwanCrystal model configurations, independently of supported graphics mode.

Preserve ordinary register/immediate/segment pushes, memory-source sampling, PUSHA’s saved entry SP, calls and interrupt frames.

## Context

The clean local checkout and inspected remote main match the baseline. The open Issue/PR collection is empty; all 50 closed entry titles were inspected without finding equivalent completed work.

The pinned [WSCPUTest report](https://github.com/FluBBaOfWard/WSCPUTest/blob/245b12c06dede4a2bb9c04c942ebca2044ba4930/README.md) describes decrement-before-value PUSH SP behavior. Its [stack experiment](https://github.com/FluBBaOfWard/WSCPUTest/blob/245b12c06dede4a2bb9c04c942ebca2044ba4930/WSCpuTest.asm#L7119) compares a pushed-and-popped SP with incoming SP minus two. The [NEC V30MZ manual, Appendix A](https://www.renesas.com/en/document/lbr/v30mztm-hardware-preliminary), documents both register encodings. Applying the experiment’s rule to `FF F4` is an explicit instruction-level inference; independently inspected per-model silicon logs are unavailable.

Correction record: replace the implementation assumption that every register source is sampled before stack decrement with the V30MZ-specific PUSH SP rule. Record the old assumption, corrected requirement, sources and rationale. Evidence-based technical corrections require no human approval or independent AI re-review; preserve the agreed goal and relevant acceptance.

Existing word-transfer tests exercise PUSH AX; the PUSHA round-trip test does not assert its saved SP slot. [Saved #49 validation](https://github.com/takahirox/wonderswan-rust/blob/9b98c69f59b736e4c31df5414844466e8ba3a099/docs/issue-49-validation.md) reports 139 core tests, 21 integration tests, one adapter test and complete Chromium suites passing. Its final packed-mode test revision has native-only evidence. These are Coordinator-reported results, not planning-time reruns.

Scope is PUSH SP sampling and necessary regression, fixture, native/Wasm/browser and documentation work. Absolute CPU timing, single-step delivery and unrelated hardware gaps remain separate work.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Correct both `54` and `FF F4` through ordinary decoding, preserving the existing stack-write path and the other push callers. Document the assumption correction and evidence limits.
- [ ] Add independent literal vectors for both encodings: SP=`2000` → stored `1FFE`; SP=`2001` → stored `1FFF`; SP=`0002` → stored `0000`; SP=`0000` → stored `FFFE`. Use mapped RAM for observable bytes; for the last case, SS=`F100` maps the destination to physical `00FFE–00FFF`. Assert little-endian bytes, final SP, subsequent POP AX, exact IP and continuation, unchanged FLAGS under contrasting inputs, unrelated registers/segments and surrounding sentinels. Expectations must not use production push helpers.
- [ ] Prove stack writes use SS despite a segment override and distinct segment values. Guard non-SP register pushes and `FF /6` memory operands whose value equals incoming SP, so operand identity determines the exception. Assert PUSHA stores entry SP=`2000` at `1FF6` and finishes at `1FF0`; retain POP/POPA, immediate/segment pushes, CALL/RET and interrupt-frame regressions.
- [ ] Cover emulated Mono/Color/SwanCrystal model configurations, supported graphics modes and runtime mode transitions on Color/Crystal. Preserve the one-clock execution component and existing fetch/word-transfer charges: with code and stack in accessible internal RAM, unprefixed `54` totals 3/4 clocks for even/odd destinations and `FF F4` totals 4/5. Verify normal Machine scheduling advances shared devices once using the returned cost. These totals preserve repository accounting, not measured absolute timing.
- [ ] Add or extend an original source-included CC0 cartridge using the existing Python/NASM fixture tooling. Native and production Chromium/Wasm checks must compare actual CPU-written stored/popped values, SP and FLAGS for both encodings on every model and fresh restart. Include a Color/Crystal mono → color → mono sequence. Clear volatile observations, invalidate retained completion and require fresh execution markers so poisoned stale-success saves cannot pass. Record actual pre-fix focused native and cartridge failures, identifying configurations reached, followed by corrected passes.
- [ ] Before merge, the Coordinator runs `python3 fixtures/build.py --check`, `python3 demo/build.py --check`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `git diff --check`. In `web`, run `npm run build:wasm`, `npm run build`, then complete `npm run test:browser` and `npm run test:compat` sequentially against the production preview. Preserve prior CPU, three-model, firmware-free startup, video/input/frame, audio/PCM, GDMA/SDMA/Hyper Voice, SRAM/EEPROM and browser save-integrity acceptance.
- [ ] Update `docs/hardware-subset.md` and relevant fixture/provenance documentation. Preserve browser-local ownership and existing firmware/provenance policies. Record actual commands, failures, resolutions, passes and unperformed checks. The Coordinator reviews the final diff against every checkbox before merge, distinguishing tests present, reported execution and untested commercial compatibility.

## Optional validation

Baseline production-Chromium discrimination, additional browser engines and additional lawfully available software. Physical-console comparisons and human gameplay are optional evidence, unperformed during planning. None requires confirmation or blocks merge.

## Required post-merge verification

None.

## Specification reconciliation

This task was authored by AI under the agreed WonderSwan-family hardware goal.
Correct erroneous technical assumptions or acceptance criteria when primary hardware
specifications establish the correction. Update this Issue and record the original
assumption, corrected requirement, primary reference and rationale in the PR.
These technical corrections require neither human approval nor an independent AI
re-review. Preserve the agreed goal and relevant pre-merge acceptance; do not weaken
requirements merely to accommodate incomplete implementation or failing tests.

This autonomous campaign has no human-approval gate. Mandatory acceptance uses
automated native and production-browser tests on the emulator's supported model
and mode configurations. Physical-console measurements and human gameplay are
optional evidence and must remain explicitly unperformed unless actually available.
Do not invent device identities, real-device results or a requirement for human
confirmation. Resolve technical errors with recorded evidence and automated checks
through the existing Coordinator workflow.
